summary: A 41-ft timber tower with an R-6 cab, built in 1967 in the Whitefish Range to replace a 1935 pole lookout; staffed in summer, with cab access that varies.

facts.design: R-6 cab on a 41-ft treated timber tower (1967); replaced a 40-ft pole tower with an L-4 cab (1935)

access.note: Public trail from a gated dirt road. Entry to the cab depends on whether the lookout is staffed; one visitor found the building locked.

visit.trail_note: Trail starts at a gated dirt road. Sources give 2.5 miles one way (Flathead Beacon) or 4.2 miles out-and-back (Trekking Wild).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Flathead Beacon calls the trail a 2.5-mile jaunt to the summit; Trekking Wild gives 4.2 miles out-and-back. The story reports both without choosing one.

corrections.proposed: R-6 cab on a 41-ft treated timber tower (1967); the L-4 cab belonged to the 40-ft pole tower of 1935
corrections.why: NHLR and firelookout.com both give an R-6 cab on the current 41-ft tower. The L-4 describes the earlier pole tower.
Both sources give the current tower as 41 feet (12.5 m). The 12.2 m figure matches the earlier 40-ft tower.

sources.title: Hiking Cyclone Lookout Trail in Flathead National Forest

notes_for_editor: Structure and dates are well corroborated (NHLR and firelookout.com agree). Staffing evidence is dated (2014 guide) or undated (NHLR); the Trekking Wild visit is undated. No fire history, NRHP nomination or rental listing found. Elevation not used: NHLR gives 6,028 ft, firelookout gives 6031 ft. Verify current season and cab access with the Flathead National Forest before publishing.
